additional_info.subject: RE: ID0418781-DC/Si-D/FR-[Y2 / P0 312567479/20] Hardware issue CRM:02679000113
additional_info.body:
Hi Maxime Maucler,
I hope you are doing well.
We have merged four cases into this one, so this case now involves four units:
pRRz0u
– P8 312547889/13
mgibgC
– P0 312567479/20
Xvtv8y
– PD 312571675/25
RFhsW1
– P0 312567479/17
As you mentioned, and based on the picture provided, it appears that the DC connector pin has experienced overheating, and one unit’s ring does not seem to hold the pins properly. There is a significant risk of further melting during future charging sessions.
As a precautionary safety measure, we strongly recommend either disabling the affected outlet or shutting down the entire charger until a thorough on-site inspection and further troubleshooting can be performed.
We have escalated this incident to our regional team for a site visit for a detailed investigation.
In the meantime, to support our analysis and help plan the next steps effectively, we kindly request the following additional information, if available:
The total kWh delivered by the affected outlet
An estimate of the total number of charging sessions performed on this outlet
Confirmation on whether a Charge Management System (CMS) is installed and active
A clear picture of the plug type label for reference
Thank you for your cooperation. We look forward to your response so we can resolve this issue promptly and ensure continued safety.
Best Regards,
Sominath Nagalgaon
eMobility Support Team
Please do not change the subject line with replying back to this email.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0418781-DC/Si-D/FR-[Y2 / P0 312567479/20] Hardware issue CRM:02679000113
additional_info.body:
Dear RC-FR Team,
This case now involves four units & customer complaints as below:
pRRz0u
– P8 312547889/13 : We observe signs of overheating on the pin of the DC1 connector (left). Could you please forward the issue to the French team for action as soon as possible?
mgibgC
– P0 312567479/20 : The DC2 connector was blocked on SCB by the Siemens France team. We observe significant signs of overheating on the left pins of the DC2 connector (right). Could you please proceed with replacing the connector as soon as possible?
Xvtv8y
– PD 312571675/25 : The ring does not seem to hold the pins properly on the DC1 connector (left). Could you please check the condition of the connector and replace it if necessary?
RFhsW1
– P0 312567479/17 : The pins of the DC1 connector (left) show signs of overheating. On the DC2 connector side (right), there’s no sign of overheating, but the ring around the pins no longer seems to hold them properly. Could you please check the condition of the connectors and replace them if necessary?
There is a significant risk of further melting during future charging sessions. As a precautionary safety measure, we strongly recommend either disabling the affected outlet or shutting down the entire charger until a thorough on-site inspection and further troubleshooting can be performed same inform to our customer as well,
